title: WTC Health Program Denies Eight Petitions to Add Ischemic Heart Disease as a Covered Condition
detail: The Administrator of the World Trade Center Health Program published a Federal Register notice denying eight petitions (024, 042, 046, 047, 051, 056, 058, and 067) requesting that ischemic heart disease be added to the List of WTC-Related Health Conditions. After reviewing the scientific literature, including material submitted by petitioners, the Administrator found insufficient evidence to support convening the program's Scientific/Technical Advisory Committee or proposing a rule change. Advocates for 9/11 survivors and responders said the denial came amid broader concerns that staffing shortages at the WTC Health Program and leadership turnover at the CDC were slowing the addition of new covered conditions even as long-term studies continue to document elevated cardiovascular and cancer risk among Ground Zero responders.

title: Steel Across America Tour Brings WTC Steel Beam to Los Angeles Ahead of 25th Anniversary
detail: The Tunnel to Towers Foundation's 'Steel Across America' tour — carrying a 16,000-pound steel beam recovered from the World Trade Center — stopped at the Frank Hotchkin Memorial Training Center in Los Angeles. Retired FDNY firefighter John LaBarbera thanked Los Angeles first responders for their mutual support, both those who traveled to Ground Zero during the 2001 rescue and recovery effort and those from New York who assisted during Southern California's January 2025 wildfires. The tour launched in lower Manhattan in May 2026 and is traveling more than 10,500 miles across 21 states and Washington, D.C., with over 35 stops, before returning to Ground Zero for the 25th anniversary commemoration on September 11, 2026.
